Additional funding may also be provided from the syndication of low-income housing tax credits. The newly constructed buildings provide rental housing affordable to low- and moderate-income households, with at least 60% of units affordable to households earning up to 80% of Area Median Income (\u001aAMI\u001a) and up to 40% of units affordable to households earning up to 120% of AMI. At least 15% of units are set aside for formerly homeless households.</span></span></p><p> </p><p><span style='font-size:10pt'>Under the proposed project, the City will sell the Disposition Area to Nehemiah Spring Creek 5B Housing Development Fund Corporation ('Sponsor') for the nominal price of one dollar per tax lot. The Sponsor will also deliver an enforcement note and mortgage for the remainder of the appraised value (\u001aLand Debt\u001a). The Sponsor will then construct three buildings containing up to 200 rental dwelling units, including one superintendent unit, on the Disposition Area.</span></p><p> </p><p><span style='font-size:10pt'>The Land Debt or the City\u001as capital subsidy may be repayable out of resale or refinancing profits for a period of at least thirty (30) years following completion of construction. The remaining balance, if any, may be forgiven at the end of the term.</span></p><p> </p><p><span style='font-size:10pt'>The appraisal and the proposed Land Disposition Agreement and Project Summary
